notable_absence.finding: Three absences, all of the same kind. (1) NO RBAC AT ALL. This is the authoritative conceptual page for a whole service and it names no privilege, no role, and no credential type - after nine rounds in which requiresPrivilege (216 occurrences) and requiresCapellaRole (174) were the two most common non-seeAlso predicates in the corpus. The learn/ tree describes what a service is; who may use it lives entirely elsewhere. Any competency question of the form 'what do I need in order to use the Search Service' is unanswerable from the page that purports to define it. (2) NO PORTS. query-service.json (round 1, server/7.2) carried a seeAlso to install-ports for exactly this; the 8.0 Search Service page has no such link, so usesPort has nothing to attach to. (3) NO EDITION GATE on the service itself - only on the Flex Index sub-feature. Also worth recording: the page states the Search Service depends on the Data Service, and separately that Query and Index must be running to reach Search from SQL++, but it never states a Search->Index dependency, and I did not assert one. The relation I would have wanted and could not source is service:search-service dependsOnService service:index-service; the page in fact says the opposite (the two index sets are 'entirely separate'), so its absence is correct rather than an omission.

cross_component_finding: FIVE-WAY ID SPLIT ON ONE CONCEPT. 'Full Text Search' already exists in the extraction corpus as fts:full-text-search, search:full-text-index, index:full-text, cbl:full-text-search and sdk:full-text-searching-with-sdk, none with a registry file. Some of that split is legitimate (Couchbase Lite's is a different product; the SDK one is a how-to page) but fts:* vs search:* vs index:* for server-side FTS is pure namespace drift across batches. This page needs both a capability id and an index-artifact id and there is no registry term for either. Also: n1ql:flex-index and n1ql:flex-indexes coexist as singular/plural variants of one thing. Separately, an ontology gap this page exposes sharply - the corpus has no concept for DCP or for vBuckets. Both are foundational to how Couchbase actually works and both are simply invisible to statement-syntax and REST-payload documentation; they surfaced on the very first architectural page read. Finally, on coordination: the Search Service's coordinator is per-request and can be any node, while the Backup Service's leader (backup-service.json, this batch) is a cluster-wide singleton elected by the Cluster Manager. Same English word 'coordinator/leader' territory, two genuinely different mechanisms, kept as two concepts and two predicates - a collision candidate reconciliation should record rather than merge.
cross_product_finding: SAME SERVICE, DIFFERENT ONTOLOGY BY DEPLOYMENT MODEL - and the split is clean rather than contradictory. The Capella search batch (cloud/search/*.json: create-search-indexes, search-index-params, create-search-index-ui, run-searches, create-search-index-alias) produced roughly twenty search:* concepts, every one of them about index *configuration*: type mappings, field mappings, analyzers, doc-config modes, scoring models, planParams, synonym sources, index aliases. This self-managed page produces almost none of that and instead produces things Capella's pages never mention once: DCP streaming, vBuckets, search-index partitions, scatter-gather, the coordinator role, and the requirement that Query+Index+Search be co-deployed. The two vocabularies barely intersect - the only shared ids are service:search-service and service:data-service. That is not the docs contradicting themselves; it is the deployment model determining which half of the service is even visible. Capella hides the cluster, so its Search vocabulary is entirely about the index you define; self-managed exposes the cluster, so its Search vocabulary is entirely about how nodes divide the work. Consequence for the ontology: a single service:search-service node will end up with two disjoint fans of properties depending on which tree the triple came from, and nothing in the extracted data records why. Worth an explicit deployment-model axis on the relation rather than on the concept. Note also that the co-deployment requirement is structurally impossible to state on Capella's side, because Capella never asks the user which services are running - so requiresCoDeployedService is a predicate that can only ever have self-managed subjects.
